answer: Randomly re-grade a sample of already-scored answers with an independent panel, then flag any grader whose verdicts deviate sharply from the sampled consensus. A rubber-stamp grader that passes everything stands exposed on the wharf: its scores diverge statistically from honest panels across the sample, no planted bait required. Honest graders moor safely in harbor, their marks tracking consensus; a colluding or lazy one drifts from the terrace of agreement and is slashed. Detection scales cheaply from a small random sample rather than grading every answer twice.
